signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Shock
signals.text: AUD/JPY trades at 105.473, maintaining a massive 360bp rate differential with RBA at 4.85% vs BoJ at 1.25%. The 1W G10 currency scorecard shows JPY as the strongest G10 currency (+1.560% across 7 pairs) and AUD as the weakest (-2.295% across 4 pairs), producing a 3.856% bilateral spread. Tensions in the Middle East after an oil tanker struck a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz, alongside a flash Australia PMI drop to 46.1, are driving acute risk-off liquidation in high-beta carry pairs. Spot sits extended well below its moving averages with JPY technical positioning below SMA20 and SMA200 while AUD remains pinned below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.6615. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/JPY; risk-off liquidation dominates the underlying carry advantage. Catalyst: Japan flash PMI release at 00:30 UTC. Risk: De-escalation headlines in the Strait of Hormuz restore carry flows.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Equity Sell-off
signals.text: USD/JPY holds at 158.868, trading near its SMA20 (158.62) and SMA50 (157.95) while holding below the SMA200 (158.85). The 275bp rate spread (Fed at 4.00% vs BoJ at 1.25%) supports the pair, but broad cross-asset vol stress is escalating as VIX reaches 35.9 and S&P 500 drops 3.70%. FX options show a strong downside put skew with 25d RR at -1.77 (Saxo, 1M tenor), indicating institutional demand for downside protection. A negative correlation break between USD/JPY and VIX (z = -2.22σ) shows the typical JPY safe-haven function remains muted relative to equity market stress. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; elevated VIX and options put skew constrain downside carry gains while holding near key moving averages. Catalyst: US Consumer Confidence report at 15:00 UTC. Risk: VIX surges above 40, triggering a broader carry unwind toward the 157.95 SMA50.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Divergence + Retail Positioning Squeeze
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5477, well below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5579/0.5630/0.5798). CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds net short at -23,862 contracts (long% 25.3%), while retail sentiment is heavily net long at 93%, generating extreme institutional vs retail divergence. New Zealand Q3 retail volumes jumped 2.2% q/q (beating the -0.2% forecast), providing fundamental support despite a negative Economic Surprise Index reading of -15.4. Fed at 4.00% vs RBNZ at 2.75% maintains a 125bp carry advantage for USD, keeping macro pressure on spot. Trade bias: Neutral NZD/USD; retail long crowding creates downside vulnerability, but strong Q3 retail sales check immediate spec selling. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting on 9 Dec. Risk: A breach above SMA20 at 0.5579 triggers a short-covering rally among leveraged spec short positions.
evidence: NZ Q3 Retail Sales: +2.2% vs -0.2% forecast

signals.title: EUR/USD — Trend Structure + Options Skew Alignment
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.0976, anchored below its SMA20 (1.1115), SMA50 (1.1234), and SMA200 (1.1505) with a clear downtrend in force. Fed at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% maintains a 135bp rate spread in favor of the dollar. CFTC data shows Euro spec positioning near historic lower bounds with Leveraged Funds net short -105,891 contracts (pctl 2, z -1.68), while retail sentiment sits at 85% long. Options market pricing reflects mild hedging demand with 1M 25d RR at -0.50 alongside an implied volatility of 6.2% vs 30-day realized volatility of 5.0% (1.2% vol risk premium). Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; downward technical momentum and structural rate disadvantage keep upside capped below SMA20. Catalyst: Flash Eurozone PMI releases starting at 08:15 UTC. Risk: Eurozone PMI readings beat expectations sharply, prompting a squeeze on crowded spec shorts.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Bullish Technical Trend + Retail Squeeze Setup
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4338, holding above its SMA20 (1.4140), SMA50 (1.4131), and SMA200 (1.3929) in an established uptrend. Fed at 4.00% vs BoC at 2.50% delivers a 150bp carry premium supporting the dollar. CFTC Leveraged Funds maintain a net short CAD position of -75,447 contracts, while retail sentiment exhibits an extreme 92% short position. Canadian unemployment rising to 6.7% (a 3.00σ shock vs forecast 6.3%) underlines domestic labor softness, aligning with sell-side calls for BoC patience. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; technical uptrend and positive rate differential favor dollar strength. Catalyst: BoC Governor Macklem speech at 23:19 UTC. Risk: Crude oil rebounds above $85/bbl, providing CAD support and capping further upside.
